scope: Offline preservation of a known map set, not supported geometry/metadata editing or a validated live restore procedure.
required_preservation: Retain exact whole-file bytes for each selected map grid and matching native-flag persistence file, plus the catalog when preserving selection/primary-backup associations. Record presence or absence, native flag, resolved path, byte length and SHA256 in a private backup manifest. Do not publish private map contents.
Retain associated primary/backup slots as distinct identities. Do not infer catalog association merely from adjacent filenames, external IDs, file mtime, access(F_OK) or available-slot allocation.

Preserve unknown grid header bytes, persistence protobuf fields/regions, catalog unknown bytes and opaque metadata. Do not decode/re-encode merely to normalize formats, zero unknown fields or regenerate IDs.
Resolve actual persistence environment path, grid paths and catalog path independently. Static defaults need not match deployed configuration.

Preserve present unresolved database/vmap/config companions provisionally with provenance, but do not label them mandatory, rebuildable or historical without caller/config evidence. Never synthesize an absent companion.

Do not restore captured shared-memory root/task bytes, pointers, fd integers, robust mutex storage or semaphore counters across process lifetimes. Their observed storage layout is not a portable serialized backup format.
preconditions_not_yet_satisfied: Obtain a non-destructive all-writer quiescence/restart protocol from the lifecycle lane, including process/shared mapping ownership. Cancellation, task-state idle and capacity repair do not satisfy this requirement.
Establish a stable cross-file/cross-region epoch for the selected files. Per-region snapshot locks and separate grid/catalog/database writers do not establish one.
Resolve state-6 producers and every relevant completion/error route. Do not interpret the value 6, a save return, ordinary AppProxy ok, or sem_post as committed map-set success.
Complete database opener/path and transaction/journal/WAL-state evidence, vmap callers and per-map config companion enumeration before declaring the backup unit complete.

Establish both grid cache and persistence buffer freshness after replacement. The known grid bulk drop covers only flags 1..11; matching persistence loads may still choose a shared buffer. Replacing files alone is insufficient.
restore_invariants: Keep a byte-identical rollback set and provenance for the pre-restore state, including unresolved companions; do not overwrite the only copy while evaluating restore feasibility.

Only once all writers and cache/mapping users are proven quiescent may an offline replacement sequence be considered. There is no established atomic multi-file replacement mechanism; any partial installation must be treated as failure requiring rollback, not a valid intermediate map set.

Verify installed whole-file SHA256 and lengths against the private backup manifest, then verify the intended catalog/native-flag associations and a genuinely disk-backed cold load. Stream-good, save/load booleans and cell digest alone are not sufficient semantic checks.

Do not promote ordinary close/rename, file visibility, cache invalidation or snapshot consistency into fsync/power-loss durability. A durability protocol and crash/power-loss validation are separate unsatisfied requirements.
remaining_runtime_checks: Under an approved device plan only: correlate writer ownership and in-flight save lifecycle with independent final-file hashes; inject per-destination open/write/close/rename failures and verify no completion indicator is misinterpreted.

Repeated foreign-owner successful buffered loads: measure process fd count and mappings, identify external cleanup and process lifetime; repeat mmap/shm_open failure cases. The static local retention observation is not a measured leak rate.
Observe all state-6 transitions with the producer identity and task/root locking; compare file visibility and errors rather than assigning a name from the numeric value.

Verify no cooperating setters/writers alter any required file or region during a backup epoch, including catalog and SQLite. Prove the chosen maintenance boundary is not merely scheduler/task acceptance.

Exercise actual cold-start selection and restored-grid load in the flow lane, checking stale grid caches, shared persistence buffers and mismatched native/external IDs independently. Include flag12 separately if the intended operation uses it.

Determine actual database path, journal mode, active transaction state and supported consistent acquisition method; ensure journal/WAL dependencies are captured as required by that observed configuration.

Confirm which vmap/config companions are read after restore, whether missing versus present files change behavior, and whether any are legitimately regenerated. Until then preserve bytes and report unresolved status.
Validate safe shutdown/restart and durability ordering on a sacrificial/test environment before any operational restore. Kernel/library, storage and power-loss behavior remain unverified here.
evidence: evidence.json:C01-C04, hash-bound focused instructions and C (decompiler output, not recovered source)
dependencies.json: conditional file roles, instruction context, path literals, ordering edges and barrier limitations
Existing immutable persistence/catalog/grid/orchestration component records; no supervisor or request-bridge implementation changed
